sourceUnderstanding.summary: The sources define a 12‑week data‑engineering learning plan with phases, exercises, and deliverables.
The AI report outlines a 12‑week data engineering learning plan with phases on SQL, Python, Airflow, warehouse modeling, and a capstone, plus optional extras.

skills.name: SQL query writing (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, window functions)
Designing star schemas and SCD type 2

evidence.excerpt: This plan takes a learner with basic spreadsheet skills to a junior data engineer level.
Learn SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, window functions and query plans. Practise on a sample retail database with at least 50 exercises. Understanding indexes is required before moving on.
Learn Python basics, then pandas for cleaning and transforming data. Write small scripts that read CSV files, validate them and load them into a database.
Build DAGs that schedule extract, transform and load steps. Learn retries, backfills and task dependencies. Every pipeline must be idempotent so a rerun never duplicates data.
Design a star schema with fact and dimension tables. Learn slowly changing dimensions (type 2) and when to denormalise.

Build an end-to-end batch pipeline: ingest daily sales files, clean them with Python, orchestrate with Airflow and load a star schema in PostgreSQL. Add data quality checks that fail the run when row counts drop by more than 20 percent. Present the pipeline with a short written design document.
- Learn dbt for SQL transformations.
- Try a streaming tool such as Kafka after the capstone.

requirements.statement: The plan must be completed in 12 weeks.
Learner should devote about 10 hours per week.
Understanding indexes is required before moving on from Phase 1.
Every pipeline must be idempotent; a rerun must never duplicate data.
Capstone project must include data quality checks that fail when row counts drop by more than 20 percent.
Capstone project deliverable: short written design document.
Complete at least 50 SQL exercises on a sample retail database.
Optional: Learn dbt for SQL transformations.
Optional: Try a streaming tool such as Kafka after the capstone.
